name: Seoul
tagline: The 1905 market where Korean street food was born, and the Bib Gourmand beef tartare right next door.

Gwangjang Market.description: Korea's oldest traditional market, since 1905, with stalls for bindaetteok, sundae, and yukhoe. Anthony Bourdain visited on 'Parts Unknown'.

Buchon Yukhoe.description: A yukhoe (Korean beef tartare) specialist next to Gwangjang Market. Bib Gourmand since 2018.

Tosokchon Samgyetang.description: Seoul's most popular samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), near Gyeongbokgung Palace, a favorite of presidents.

Myeongdong Kyoja.description: Hand-cut kalguksu noodles and mandu, a family recipe since 1966 right in Myeongdong. Michelin Guide.

Mingles.description: Contemporary Korean haute cuisine from chef Kang Mingoo in Gangnam. Three Michelin stars.

Jungsik.description: Chef Yim Jung-sik's avant-garde Korean cuisine reinterprets traditional dishes with modern technique, in Apgujeong. Two Michelin stars.

La Yeon.description: Korean royal court cuisine served atop the Shilla Hotel, with views over Namsan. Two Michelin stars.

Kwonsooksoo.description: Korean haute cuisine built around mandu (dumplings) elevated into a tasting menu, in Gangnam. Two Michelin stars.

Soigné.description: French technique fused with seasonal Korean ingredients in Cheongdam. Two Michelin stars.

Evett.description: A tasting menu blending Korean pantry with Nordic sensibility, in the Yeonnam-dong neighborhood. Promoted to two Michelin stars in 2025.

Kojima.description: An edomae-style sushi counter in Cheongdam, a benchmark for high-end Japanese dining in Seoul. Two Michelin stars.

Balwoo Gongyang.description: The only restaurant run directly by Korea's Jogye Buddhist order, serving vegetarian temple cuisine (sachal eumsik) next to Jogyesa Temple. One Michelin star.

Byeokje Galbi.description: A hanwoo beef-rib galbi institution since 1986, using cattle raised on its own Pocheon farm and charcoal grills built into every table.

Congdu.description: Contemporary banchan-heavy hanjeongsik near Gyeongbokgung Palace. Michelin Guide Bib Gourmand.

Hadongkwan.description: Hanwoo beef-bone gomtang soup served since 1939 in the heart of Myeongdong, with the original recipe and furniture preserved. Bib Gourmand.

Yongsusan.description: Gaeseong-style hanjeongsik served as a full course of dozens of banchan, named 'Best Korean Restaurant' by the Seoul city government.

Sanchon.description: A vegetarian Buddhist temple-food restaurant in Insadong, founded by a former monk, with traditional performances during dinner.

Osegyehyang.description: A pioneer of vegan jjajangmyeon and other Korean-Chinese dishes in Anguk, a long-running fixture of Seoul's vegetarian scene.

Woo Lae Oak.description: Seoul's oldest still-operating Pyongyang-style naengmyeon (cold noodle) restaurant, opened in 1946. Bib Gourmand.

Pildong Myeonok.description: Bibim naengmyeon served with the noodles' own starchy cooking water instead of beef broth, one of the five 60-plus-year Pyongyang naengmyeon houses recognized by the Michelin Guide.

Ojang-dong Heungnamjip.description: Spicy sweet-potato-noodle Hamheung-style naengmyeon since 1953, opened by refugees from the North during the Korean War.

Sunhee's Bindaetteok.description: A landmark stall inside Gwangjang Market famous for its bindaetteok (mung bean pancake), yukhoe, and mayak gimbap.

Sindang-dong Tteokbokki Town.description: The tteokbokki alley born in 1953 when Ma Bok-rim began selling spicy rice cakes; it shot to national fame after a 1996 gochujang TV ad.

Jangchungdong Jokbal Golmok.description: A historic alley of jokbal (braised pig's trotters) shops in Jangchung-dong, where competing storefronts have guarded the same recipe for decades.

Wonjo Yeongyang Center.description: Opened in Myeongdong in 1960 with an electric rotisserie for whole birds, a pioneer of Korean roast chicken and of chicken delivery from 1968 onward.

Kyochon Chicken.description: Chain founded in 1991 that popularized soy-garlic Korean fried chicken, today one of the country's largest.

Noryangjin Fisheries Wholesale Market.description: Seoul's largest wholesale fish market, where Anthony Bourdain had fresh octopus for breakfast on 'No Reservations'.

Garak Market.description: A large wholesale market in Songpa-gu where Bourdain sampled banchan, live seafood, and maeuntang stew on 'Parts Unknown'.

Mapo Jeong Daepo.description: A Mapo-style galmaegisal (pork skirt meat) grill house Anthony Bourdain visited for a 'Parts Unknown' segment on Korean office 'hoesik' culture.

Fritz Coffee Company.description: The flagship roaster of Korean specialty coffee, set in a restored 1960s hanok in Mapo-gu; a touchstone of Seoul's coffee revival.

Anthracite Coffee Roasters.description: A specialty roaster housed in a former shoe factory in Hapjeong, its roasting room visible through industrial glass walls.

Center Coffee.description: A pioneer of Seoul's specialty-coffee scene, with a rotating single-origin pour-over menu and a flagship in Seongsu-dong.

Onion Seongsu.description: A cafe set inside a 1970s former metal factory in Seongsu-dong, famous for its fresh-baked bread and its endlessly photographed industrial look.

Daelim Changgo.description: A former Seongsu-dong warehouse turned cafe-gallery with soaring ceilings and art installations; one of the first cafes to go viral and put the neighborhood on the map.

Suyeon Sanbang.description: Seoul's first traditional hanok tea house, the former home of writer Lee Tae-jun in Seongbuk-dong, designated a folk cultural property.

Le Chamber.description: A Cheongdam-dong speakeasy entered by pulling the right book off a bookshelf; on Asia's 50 Best Bars list every year since 2016.

Alice Cheongdam.description: An Alice in Wonderland-inspired speakeasy reached through a secret door in a flower shop; ranked No. 13 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025.

Vatos Urban Tacos.description: Founded in 2011 in an Itaewon back alley by three Korean-Americans, the pioneer of Korean-Mexican fusion in Seoul (kimchi carnitas fries, bulgogi tacos).

Isaac Toast.description: A grilled-toast sandwich chain born in Myeongdong in 1989, a classic of Korean street breakfast.

Gogung.description: Jeonju-style bibimbap served in a sizzling stone bowl, with a heavily visited branch in Insadong.

Jaha Sonmandu.description: Handmade mandu dumplings in Buam-dong, in a garden house at the foot of Mount Bugaksan; recommended by the Michelin Guide.

Tongin Market.description: A traditional market beside Gyeongbokgung Palace famous for its 'Dosirak Cafe' concept, where visitors buy brass coins to assemble a lunchbox from the market's stalls.

Eulji Myeonok.description: One of Seoul's five long-running Pyongyang naengmyeon houses, holding a Michelin Bib Gourmand, in Euljiro.

Nokdu Jip.description: A historic haunt near Yonsei University, a meeting point for generations of students over mung-bean pancakes and makgeolli rice wine.

Coffee Libre.description: A pioneering specialty roaster in Seoul since 2009, based in Yeonnam-dong, an early landmark of Korea's third-wave coffee movement.

Ryunique.description: A French-Korean tasting menu from chef Lee Won-il in Cheongdam-dong. One Michelin star.

Passion 5.description: A bakery, patisserie, and dessert-bar complex from the SPC group in Hannam-dong, opened in 2010 as a showcase for modern Korean pastry.

Maple Tree House.description: An upscale Korean BBQ chain heavily recommended to foreign visitors, with a longtime branch in Itaewon.

Charles H.description: A classic cocktail bar inside the JW Marriott Dongdaemun Square, a regular on the Asia's 50 Best Bars lists.

Sanwonga.description: A grill house specializing in high-grade hanwoo beef in Gangnam, a fixture of Seoul business dining.

Gwanghwamun Jip.description: A 60-plus-year spot near Gwanghwamun famed for kongnamul gukbap (bean-sprout soup) and bulgogi, a classic among Seoul office workers.

Sulbing.description: A chain born in 2013 that popularized modern milk-and-injeolmi bingsu (shaved ice) across Korea, with a landmark Hongdae location.

Jihwaja.description: A Joseon royal court cuisine restaurant near Deoksugung Palace, serving elaborate banchan tasting menus.

Goryeo Samgyetang.description: A popular alternative to Tosokchon for samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup), near Insadong and Gwanghwamun.

Layered.description: A Yeonnam-dong bakery celebrated for its scones, part of the new wave of artisan baking that has reshaped Seoul's cafe scene.

Anam.description: Pork and rice soup (dwaeji gukbap) near Korea University, added to the Michelin Guide Seoul as a new Bib Gourmand in 2024.

Linus' BBQ.description: A Texas-style smokehouse in the Itaewon area, a landmark of the American barbecue scene that has grown in Seoul.

Eulmildae.description: A Pyongyang naengmyeon house that opened as a small shop in 1971, one of Seoul's five historic houses with over half a century in business.

Osulloc Tea House.description: The flagship tea house of Jeju green-tea brand Osulloc in Insadong, serving matcha-based desserts and drinks.

BBQ Chicken.description: A chain founded in Seoul in 1995 that popularized olive-oil fried chicken, today one of the world's largest Korean chicken franchises.
